Don't do it!
Aug 2024 • Family
I would not do this cruise again, and would not recommend it. The food was VERY average, and we were served dry chicken with stale chips, pork spare ribs with stale chips and soggy lettuce, tinned tuna with tomato and soggy lettuce, garlic bread and water melon, while every other table on board seemed to get quite nice looking Vietnamese food, with a cooker on their tables. The cocktails all seemed to contain the same alcohol with some different flavourings, heavily dosed with sugar syrup. The service was not good. The entertainment was an enthusiastic professional singer, interspersed with some even more enthusiastic (and loud) karaoke from fellow passengers. The final bit of the cruise did offer some excellent views of the lights of the city from the river, which was very good.

So much food!
Aug 2022
You can buy any river dinner cruise package at any travel agency in the city center. This one is 400,000 dong per person or about USD17. Admission is from 5:30-7:30. There was a lot of food, very healthy and delicious. They had us choose from 2 set menu upon purchasing the tickets. There are singers but the songs are all Vietnamese, they allow drunk passengers to sing as well. The city view and lights were stunning. The ship started moving from 8pm until 9pm. For our package, the drinks are not included so make sure to bring cash. Overall, the experience was very good and we highly recommend you try it when in Saigon.

Solid 3.5* affair!
Sep 2019
We were invited to a dinner cruise by our close friends in Vietnam. The process of boarding was both smooth and painless. It felt very much like a huge tent at an Oktoberfest in Germany.

We ordered our food and drinks and before long our 'tent' set sail on the Saigon River.

There was entertainment from the stage. Food and service was very good. The waiters and the designated station chief were very attentive and would whisk away before you could say 'una mas cerveza'...oops...wrong country!

As we chug along on the Saigon River we had the accompaniment of music and entertainment. It was a very pleasant evening spent eating, drinking, and more importantly, good old fashioned socializing without any modern technology. Loved that!

Recommended......if you've read what I wrote...lol!

Nothing Special !!
Jan 2018 • Friends
A group of seven of us had dinner at this ship on 19th January 2018. The three tiered ship was beautifully lit and was in the form of an open mouthed shark. We were one of the first to arrive and were allocated seats on the top deck. Since it was dark there was nothing much you could see in the Saigon river except for large barges transporting various goods and a few other ships like this one catering to visitors.
Our dishes had been pre-ordered by the touring company that hosted us. The food that was served to us was average and nothing to write home about. There was some singing in the central stage by some artistes – which again was not much more than average.
All in all it was ok. But we enjoyed a good drink of beer and sang “happy birthday” to one in our group.

Floating Restaurant in HCM City? Thinking Out Loud Review
Apr 2017 • Friends
First, we went to Tau Ben Nghe river cruise before 8pm (started time) and we were so surprised the ladies and gentlemen whom we met wearing with their traditional white sailor boat uniform. I thought they were officers in the boat, but no way they were waiters and assistants. Look confusing when i saw one of the officers. I thought that night was amazing and could have enjoyed our night, fortunately not. 

Having been waiting for so long with our food to eat, we met some waiters and waitresses and asked them if they could lend us a menu book, but the guy we talked to seemed didn't care and failed to show us...Minutes later that boring night, I thought he carried a menu was for our table...hmmn he gave it to the next table. Probably, he noticed that they were bunch of families and we're four only. The question is: who arrived and settled down first? Isn't it rude? We should have entertained first before others. Anyway, without a doubt we walked out without telling them and moved to the next cruise (just for few meters away on foot) and stepped in at Saigon by night: Traditional Dinner Cruise.

Hoping for the best night...it seemed peaceful and the air was so fresh...feeling happy to find a new place to dine -in...The waiters looks so different and could feel the atmosphere of the restaurant. I thought 'this is it!' The waiters and waitresses seemed so attentive and was able to speak few english words. Not bad as I thought! When we asked for a menu, they gave us rightaway. We found out they have English and VN languages written on the menu...so feeling confident to order our 3 main courses - local seafood hot pot, fried frog and chicken with butter and onions. Of course, cooked rice is also available when you need it. In short, we tried their food and drinks.

While we were eating dinner, some local singers tried their best to entertain their customers...feeling overwhelmed when a middle aged lady sangs 1980-90s English songs. For me, too old to hear them, but in fairness one of them could sings songs in Chinese, VN and little English. That was cool, but it would be great if they could hire young and talented singers from other countries to spice up the night with families and friends.

The night seemingly appeared so smoothly as they announced the boat was going to side by side of the river in Saigon. In the beginning, I thought they could take us further. Later, we found out they could only take their customers to a 400-500 meters trip side by side...that was why i wonder it only took an hour dinner in the cruise per trip.

With regard to the food, it seems delicious when it comes to fried foods. i think it is remarkable, even my 6 year old daughter could enjoy fried chicken and frog without knowing what the food she ate once was a frog meat. However, the seafood hotpot is not that delicious as i expected. That was not so tasty and meaty content, that's why it made me wonder why they call it - "Traditional Dinner Cruise." 

To add insult to injury, the price of the food ranges from 8 usd (minimum) to 25 usd or more, which can, in fact, be found somewhere in the streets or small restaurants in Saigon and they are more delicious than this place. Duh! We were aware of the pricy food (315,000 vnd/serving) especially the untasty hotpot. What made me surprisingly disappointed was the entrance fee (almost 2 dollars/person) and the 1% service charge of the total cost (because i used Atm card???? What?). This is crazy! It was not included in the untasty food produced by Binh Quoi company? What on earth!

What i learnt from this trip? 1) Better go to Hard Rock cafe and enjoy your dinner and music there till night. 2) Be aware before you go to every places in VN. Fill your knowledge with information. My simple tips before you dine-in. Bring your own wet/dry tissue or bottled water. Remember every 'thing' you move/touch is a penny to their pocket, or sometimes the price is 2-5 times higher than any convenience stores. Therefore, be careful! Hope you enjoy reading my honest to goodness of my latest review. (April 5, 2017)
